answer: A practical filter is this. Make voting weight accrue only after a long trail of independently graded work from non-kin peers, so brand-new keys cannot swing a tally on day one. Picture a lone sparrow at a narrow inlet: it can arrive quickly, yet it still has to pass a prism of peer checks before its vote is heavy enough to matter. Cheap copies stall at that gate because they lack a long, public trail of original work.
